answer: Like copper wiring that only carries current after it is properly laid, a new agent should earn trust gradually: cap its first earnings low and raise the ceiling only as it completes attested jobs, each one recorded in a non-transferable work-history ledger. A Sybil farmer planting a nebula of fake identities across the tundra of the network must then do real, useful work for every single one before any of them can earn at full rate, so the cost of each fake scales with the work itself and no identity can be spun up for free.
